content.title: Branches: Isolate One Piece of Work
content.hook: Imagine five engineers all editing the same main line of history at once.
content.context:
Every unfinished experiment is now mixed together.

Branches give each piece of work its own line.

Think of them like this:

```text
                 feature/search
                /
main ---------A----------------D
                 \
                  feature/cart
```

The exact internal model is more precise than this drawing, but the useful idea is simple:

**A branch gives a named line of work.**
goals: Understand branches as independent lines of project history that let engineers work on a change without treating the shared main line as their personal scratch space.

content.title: Create a branch
content.text:
A common command is:

```bash
git switch -c feature/cart-summary
```

The important part is not the exact spelling.

The important idea is:

> “I am creating a separate line for this piece of work.”

content.question: Why is a branch useful before changing the cart summary?

options.text: It keeps the work isolated from the main line until you are ready to integrate it.
It makes the code run faster.

feedback.correct: A branch creates a safer place for focused work and review.
feedback.incorrect: A branch creates a safer place for focused work and review.

activities.title: Branch names should explain the work

content.title: Branch names should explain the work
content.text:
Prefer:

```text
feature/cart-summary
fix/empty-search-state
chore/update-docs
```

over:

```text
test
stuff
new
johns-branch
```

The exact naming convention can vary between teams. The shared principle is clarity.

content.title: Switch back
content.text:
Suppose you finish your experiment and return to the main line.

```bash
git switch main
```

Now your current working context points at the main branch again.

activities.title: A branch is not a hiding place

content.question:
You create a feature branch and make a terrible change.

Does the branch guarantee the change can never affect anything else?

options.text: Yes. Branches make code permanently harmless.
No. A branch isolates history, but you still have to review and integrate changes carefully.
Yes. Git deletes bad code automatically.
No because branches are just folders.

feedback.correct: Branches create separation. They do not replace engineering judgment.
feedback.incorrect: Branches create separation. They do not replace engineering judgment.
